title: StakeholderMap
description: How much power each stakeholder holds over one piece of work. A binding, not a container: it does not decide who is on a project (a project references the resources it involves directly, stakeholders among them); it adds the one thing that belongs to neither end. A resource is declared once and used across many projects; the power it holds is particular to each, so it is stored on the link rather than on either side. Scoring is optional on purpose: identifying a stakeholder and assessing their power are separate acts, and an entry with no score is one somebody has declared but not yet placed, which is a state worth holding rather than one that loses the entry.

scope.description: The work this map is about. A reference rather than a fixed Project field, so a programme or an operation can carry one without a second near-identical kind. A kind rule refuses a scope that is not work.

items.description: One stakeholder: a Resource or a beneficiary group, exactly one of the two (a kind rule; TAXONOMY.md D42).

resource.description: The catalogue entry being scored. It need not be one the work references: a party with power over a project is often not part of it.

group.description: A beneficiary group being scored, in place of a resource: the people the work is for are stakeholders too, and naming the group here saves recording it a second time as a Resource.

stake.description: What this party cares about in this work, in one sentence. Influence and interest say how much; this says what. Not who they are, which the resource or group already says.

owner.description: The role that owns the relationship with this stakeholder, as a reference to a catalogue role or an external one. Never a person. Accountability, like a risk's owner; the channels and timing of engagement are planning.

influence.description: How much this stakeholder can change what happens. Absent until assessed.

interest.description: How much this stakeholder cares what happens. Absent until assessed.

tier.description: Primary stakeholders are directly affected by the work; secondary ones indirectly (Clarkson, 1995). A separate question from influence and interest, whose grid gives the engagement approach (Mendelow).
